# Contents The Philippine Council for Health Research and Development (PCHRD) is one of the three sectoral councils of the Department of Science and Technology (DOST).
It is a forward-looking, partnership-based national body responsible for coordinating and monitoring research activities in the country.
The DOST-PCHRD provides support at every stage of health research.
In collaboration with international partners and local partners through the Philippine National Health Research System (PNHRS), the Council is committed to advance health research in the Philippines.
The DOST-PCHRD as the recognized lead provider of research-based solutions and innovations to address health system needs by 2028.

We are committed to serve, within the highest standards of professionalism, within our core competency and available resources, in accordance to customer requirements, and in adherence to applicable requirements and towards continual improvement, the following: • formulation of strategies, policies, plans, and programs for S&T in health; • programming and allocation of government funds, and generation of external funds for R&D; and • monitoring of R&D projects.
As the national coordinating body for health research, we provide central direction, leadership and coordination of health research activities.

To achieve this, we are committed to do the following: • Formulate agenda, plans, policies, and strategies for health research • Mobilize resources to support health research • Develop and strengthen capacity for health research • Support the development of affordable, accessible,and quality S&T-based solutions and innovations • Ensure the dissemination and utilization of health research outputs • Monitor and evaluate health research activities • Establish linkages and partnerships with local and international organizations • Promote good governance among health research organizations through efficient, effective, transparent, and ethical health research management system.

The updated NUHRA for 2023 to 2028 was launched during the opening ceremonies of the 16th PNHRS Week celebration at the Summit Hotel, Tacloban City on 10 August 2023.

Spearheaded by the PNHRS Research Agenda Management Committee (RAMC), the development of the updated document involved regional consultations, and gathered inputs from a variety of research stakeholders.
From these consultations, a total of 170 health research priorities were identified and were consolidated into themes and sub-themes.

• Disease Management; • Halal in Health; • Health Security, Emergency, and Disaster Risk Management; • Health Technology and Innovation; • Health of Vulnerable Populations; • Health Promotion; • Health Systems Strengthening towards UHC; • Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health; • Mental Health; • Nutrition and Food Security; and • Sexual and Reproductive Health.
The PNHRS held a strategic planning workshop for 2023-2028 on 28-30 September 2023 at the Heritage Hotel Manila, Pasay City.

It was attended by the PNHRS Governing Council, PNHRS Steering Committee, PNHRS Technical Working Committee Chairs and Secretariats, and representatives from the 17 Regional Health Research Development Consortia including BARMM.

The three-day workshop, facilitated by Ms. Ramonesa Ricardo, gathered everyone to collaborate in improving the capacity of the System in delivering its mandate and identify new directions or objectives for the improved performance of PNHRS.

Specifically, the workshop aims to 1) Develop plans, programs, and activities that will be implemented by PNHRS and its Committees in the next five (5) years; 2) Reassess and reevaluate the PNHRS Strategy Map and Scorecard 2017-2022, its existing programs and accomplishments vis-à-vis set goals, objectives, and strategies; 3) Revisit the roles and responsibilities of PNHRS committees and its secretariat; and 4) Develop the PNHRS Strategy Map and Plans for 2023-2028.
A Post-Strategic Planning meeting will be set to meticulously review and validate the draft strategic plan.
Subsequently, the plan will undergo the approval process by the PNHRS Steering Committee, Governing Council, and implementing institution heads.
Upon approval, it will be deployed to the TWCs and regions, and translated into annual plans.

The Tuklas Lunas® Program is the drug discovery and development program of the DOST and DOST-PCHRD which envisions to “produce world-class medicines derived from the Philippine biodiversity, leveraging on local expertise”.

Building on the experience and successes of the National Integrated Research Program on Medicinal Plants (NIRPROMP) which produced lagundi and sambong herbal drugs now valued to be a PhP 1 billion industry, Tuklas Lunas aims to further tap into the potential of Philippine biodiversity as sources of drug candidates, contribute to addressing local need for more safe, effective, affordable and accessible locally-developed health products; and to the growth of the local natural products and pharmaceutical industry.

Recognizing that significant resources are needed to bring one (1) successful drug candidate from early discovery to commercialization, the Tuklas Lunas program has adopted a strategic framework that pursues two tracks of development: (1) Herbal (Biodiversity/Folkloric) track: development of standardized herbal drugs, (2) Drug (Synthesis/Pure Compound) track: the identification of high-value compounds that can be offered for early licensing for further development as drugs.
In the process, several outputs may be produced such as functional food, standardized herbal supplements, standardized herbal drugs, and pure drug candidate compounds.

• Building institutional and human capacity for discovery and development of natural products through R&D grants; • Developing bioresources (unique in the regions) into natural products; and • Bringing candidate substances/compounds to a stage where they are sufficiently de-risked and ripe for early licensing (not necessarily for full product development).

Building on the program’s previously completed projects, the three component projects of USC-TLDC Phase II intended to continue the discovery of cardiometabolic bioactives from various plants in Central Philippines as complementary medicine for the treatment, control, or prevention of hyperglycemia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and hypercholesterolemia.
In 2023, the team developed a plant formulation with good pharmacopoeial results and retention of alpha-glucosidase inhibition and glucose uptake activity and alpha-glucosidase inhibition.
These outcomes offer a promising foundation for future up-scale manufacturing.

The Central Mindanao University - Tuklas Lunas Development Center (CMU-TLDC) explores the potential of local fern species for the development of skin ointments.

Initiated in 2022, the project entitled, “Pre-Clinical Studies and Scale Up Formulation of Anti-Inflammatory PharmaFern Ointments,” aims to assess the industrial applicability of anti-inflammatory PharmaFern ointments developed from two bioactive fern species.

Together with the UP-Manila College of Pharmacy, the CMU-TLDC pursues the project through the conduct of two studies: (1) the first study will propagate the two identified fern species and evaluate the anti-inflammatory potential of the extracts and the formulated ointments; while (2) the second study will conduct pilot scale manufacturing of the anti-inflammatory ointments.

To date, the project team was already able to identify two fern extracts to be nontoxic with significant anti-inflammatory activities in terms of in vitro inhibition of cyclooxygenase and carrageenan-induced paw edema assay.
From these extracts, ointment products were developed and have been submitted for patent or utility model grant.
Initial user acceptability studies show that the ointment is generally acceptable in terms of look, smell, color, and packaging.

Currently, the research team is continuing the pilot scale manufacturing of the ointment, paw edema assay to assess the anti-inflammatory effect of the product in mice, and the production of ointments in preparation for Phase 1 of clinical trials.
The project started last 1 September 2022, and is expected to be completed on 31 March 2025 with a total allocated budget of PhP 22,357,091.00.
Seaweeds are widely acknowledged as rich sources of bioactive compounds and exhibit considerable chemical diversity.
Despite these attributes, seaweeds in the Philippines remain underutilized and lack significant economic value.
This project, centered on Panay Island, specifically aims to evaluate the potential health benefits and safety of wines derived from brown, green, and red seaweeds.
Led by Mr. Hilario S.

Taberna and implemented by the Iloilo Science and Technology University in collaboration with DOST-PCHRD, the project team successfully formulated three (3) optimized seaweed wine concoctions, conducted safety assays and physico-chemical tests, and evaluated sensory characteristics.
Preliminary findings indicate that seaweed wines boast higher antioxidant and antihyperlipidemic properties compared to commercially available wines.

Upon successful commercialization, this project envisions offering more affordable and healthier wine options for the Filipino market, while contributing valuable scientific data on Turbinaria spp., Ulva spp., and Acanthophora spicifera .
Furthermore, it aspires to strengthen the seaweed industry in Northern Iloilo, generating additional livelihood opportunities for coastal communities.

The project has garnered widespread recognition, being featured in various platforms such as Mabuhay Pilipinas of Radyo Pilipinas Radio Program, Manila Bulletin, and DOST's Regional and National Science and Technology Week.
The project, led by Dr. Leslie Michelle M.
Dalmacio, seeks to enhance the health of HIV-infected individuals by developing a Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB)-based health-promoting product.
This product aims to serve as an adjunct therapy for managing HIV patients with metabolic complications.

Key achievements of the project include obtaining data on antibiotic susceptibility of probiotic strains, conducting whole genome sequencing of two probiotic strains, optimizing studies for probiotic strains and probiotic + prebiotic combinations, and experimenting on product shelf life and stability under different storage conditions.

This project is implemented in collaboration with UP College of Medicine, National Institutes of Health Manila, UP Diliman Institute of Biology and BIOTECH-UPLB with a total budget of Php 23,122,808.88 Additionally, the project team presented their preliminary results at the 30th Federation of Asian and Oceanian Biochemists and Molecular Biologists (FAOBMB) Conference in Bangkok, Thailand, held from November 22-25, 2023.

Ongoing Project The Nutrition and Food Safety Program endeavors to tackle prevalent human nutrition challenges in the country, encompassing issues like micronutrient and macronutrient deficiencies, overnutrition, nutrition-related diseases, and emerging concerns in food safety.

Through leveraging science, technology, and innovation, the program is dedicated to identifying pathways and seizing opportunities to offer solutions that enhance the health of Filipinos by promoting proper nutrition and ensuring the safety of their food.
Officially launched in March 2022 as a new priority program area within R&D Management, this initiative garnered 18 proposals in response to the 2023 Call for Proposals.

In the next years, the program will continue in its commitment to integrating nutrition and food safety trends while actively monitoring research gaps in lesser-explored areas of nutrition-related diseases and food safety issues.
Simultaneously, efforts will be intensified to strengthen collaborations both locally and internationally.
HAPPY Senior Citizens is a research and development program that investigates the nutrition and health concerns of elderly Filipinos.
It is composed of four component projects that delve into various areas, such as body composition, cognition function, and functional foods.

The project entitled, “Development and Pilot-Scale Production of Innovation Food Products for Older Male and Female Filipinos,” under this program aims to develop two food products that will contain the recommended nutrients needed by older persons, and determine the effect of consuming the said products towards their muscle strength and physical performance.
Specifically, the project aims to develop one beverage and one snack food, utilizing mature green tomatoes (MGTs) which are known to contain Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA).
GABA, an inhibitory neurotransmitter, known to cause several health benefits such as providing support to the immune and nervous systems.
To date, the project team already tested the use of MGT powder on several food products such as biscuits, chicken nuggets, skinless longganisa, and tomato sauce.
The team was also able to develop a prototype of the high-protein beverage for enteral formula which will be used for pilot-scale production during the second year implementation of the project.
Supported by DOST and monitored by the DOST-PCHRD, the project received a total allocation of Php 9,036,790.22.

The project entitled, "Development and Effectiveness of Fully Automated Conversational Agents (Chatbots) for Enhancing Public Mental Health," focused on the creation of fully automated conversational agents, or chatbots, designed to champion mental well-being and alleviate psychological distress within the public domain.
In 2023, the project successfully leveraged innovative technology to provide accessible and timely assistance to those in need.
The product of this project are two applications: Gabay and SIBOL.
Gabay is a supportive companion that understands the unique needs of its users.

Gabay is a mobile mental health application and a compassionate companion committed to acknowledging, empowering, and supporting individuals diagnosed with depression and anxiety disorders tailored specifically for the Filipino context.
On the other hand, SIBOL will be the first Filipino-made mobile app developed specifically to address general psychological distress.
The app includes features that will enhance mental health literacy, journaling, and mood tracking.
It also promotes interpersonal connections through communication cards and acts of kindness.

Aimed to comprehensively understand the mental health landscape among the youth in the Province of Tarlac, the project engaged the Provincial Government of Tarlac, Department of Health (DOH), Local Government Units, Rural Health Units, and Sanguniang Kabataan (SK) Federations in the province that fostered a holistic approach to the study, ensuring a better understanding of the mental health status and available resources for the youth.
In 2023, the study involved 400 participants, mostly 18-year-olds attending school and coming from families with monthly incomes between Php 10,000 to 20,000.
The results revealed that over half of the participants struggled with mild to extremely severe depression, whereas 45.75% displayed a standard level of mental health.

Findings also suggest that there are prevalent mental health challenges among Tarlac's youth, indicating that nearly 75% reported experiencing anxiety levels ranging from moderate to extremely severe.
Additionally, 40% of the participants grappled with similar levels of stress.
These results, now integral baseline data, are poised to play a pivotal role in informing policies and guidelines developed by the Local Government Unit.
Moreover, it will serve as a foundation for the creation of targeted programs addressing the specific mental health needs of Tarlac's youth.

In a bid to revolutionize addiction and depression treatments, the program entitled, "Novel Approaches to Treatment of Addiction and Depression using Animal Models" explores pharmacological and behavioral interventions.

46 The Philippines, due to its topographic location, stands among the nations most vulnerable to natural catastrophes and climatic impacts.

Understanding pollen dynamics is crucial for addressing health challenges, especially allergies, which affect a significant portion of the population.
Allergies stemming from airborne pollen can lead to conditions such as allergic rhinitis, asthma, and atopic dermatitis.

By studying the seasonality, characterization, and allergenicity of airborne pollen in Ilocos Norte, this project aims to address health-related problems and educate the public on allergies, their potential causes, and the plant sources of pollen allergens that may adversely affect their health.
In 2023, the project revealed that the dominant airborne pollen sources in the region are mulberry, grasses, malunggay, Talisay, myrtle, Agoho, and aratilis.

Pollen sensitivity studies underscored a notable prevalence of allergic conditions, particularly in response to carabao mango and Indian mango pollen, with allergic rhinitis emerging as the most frequently reported condition.
Moreover, a gender-based analysis indicated a higher prevalence of self-reported allergic diseases among females.

Contributing to these findings, the project identified 220 plant species in semi-urban areas of Ilocos Norte, while urban vegetation surveys in Batac and Laoag revealed 144 plant species, mostly herbs.
Meanwhile, research on soil heavy metal concentration demonstrated compliance with safety limits across all vegetation locations.

Web-based application incorporating the human security profile per region in the country By adopting a multidimensional approach and creating a detailed human security profile, the project aims to develop data-driven solutions addressing daily insecurities, economic challenges, and other issues Filipinos encounter in the post-pandemic period.

In minimally invasive surgery, the operation consists of a variety of techniques that cause less damage than open surgery, reducing the risk of complications.
One of the first types used is laparoscopy, a procedure done through one or more small incisions using small tubes and tiny cameras and surgical instruments.
Though this technique is beneficial to patients, the strain it induces to surgeons is noticeable.

Such operations consist of a remarkable time for operating surgeons to set-up and prepare all the necessary instruments and make incisions to start, the long operating procedures give the doctors muscle pains in their hands, back, and legs.
In response to this, Dr. Deogracias Alberto is developing an Energized Reusable Laparoscopic Blunt Dissector (ERLBD) that will reduce operating time and consumables used in an operation.
It is made of a single piece of metal which eliminates risk of foreign bodies being retained due to the detachable part of the instruments.

During the Year 2 implementation, the project has completed most of its target activities including the completion of all benchtop trials and collation of data in preparation for the ex vivo trials involving porcine livers and gallbladder.
All results have been statistically analyzed by the statistician.
The project completed 87.5% of the Year 2 activities, and is currently awaiting the approval of their ethics application for the ex vivo trials.
The ERLBD will lead to a safer, lesser cost and ergonomic surgery.
Collectively, it is envisioned that this will reduce overall morbidity and mortality in laparoscopic surgeries.

In 2014, an international consortium was formed to find new treatments for X-Linked Dystonia Parkinsonism (XDP).

This global coalition, termed the Collaborative Center for X-Linked Dystonia-Parkinsonism (CCXDP) consisting of scientists and physicians from around the world, works in close partnership with neurology experts and patient advocates in the Philippines.

As part of the CCXDP network, Filipino investigators continue to lead new initiatives, including advanced neuroimaging of XDP patients, detailed clinical studies of disease manifestation, and the establishment of the first human brain tissue repository in the Philippines.

Even though genetic studies indicate that XDP most likely represents a founder mutation that has occurred within the Panay population, the actual mutation frequency and how widely it is carried among individuals in the Philippines remain unknown.
To address this gap, the investigators aim to characterize the genetic prevalence of XDP in the Philippines.

In collaboration with the CCXDP of the Massachusetts General Hospital (Harvard Medical School) and Philippine Genome Center, the project will use randomly selected biobanked de-identified residual dried blood spots, or rDBS, from the Philippine Newborn Screening Program.

The characterization of the genetic prevalence of the causative gene will provide a better understanding of the burden of disease in the country, as well as help decision-makers to determine where investments in healthcare should be targeted for such a rare disease.

To date, Dr. Cutiongco-dela Paz’ team completed the retrieval, sampling, and processing of the total target number of male rDBS, as well as the procurement of major laboratory equipment needed for the semi-automation process of genotyping of rDBS.
The team is actively working on the genotyping assay of the collected rDBS samples with almost 40% of the total assays done.
DNA extraction of disease-specific changes (DSC-1)-positive cards were performed and were transferred to CCXDP for further genetic testing.
By the end of implementation, the outputs of the study can serve as a reference for further research, clinical guidelines, and public health policymaking concerning XDP.
A similar workflow may also be developed, tested, and validated for application to other rare diseases.
Ultimately, the findings are envisioned to lead to the improvement of clinical management of this uniquely Filipino rare disease.
In the past decade, the Philippines recorded a high incidence rate of HIV infection predominantly affecting the younger, and economically-productive population.
This poses an alarming development of HIV-related metabolic and neurocognitive complications as seen in chronically-infected Filipino patients.

While antiretroviral therapy (ART) is now available for HIV-positive patients, ART cannot fully eradicate the virus in various reservoir sites (i.e., brain, bone marrow, lymph nodes, and gut), which leads to a continuous cycle of inflammation and failure of the immune system.
This immune dysregulation results in serious non-AIDS events (SNAEs) such as neurocognitive dysfunction, metabolic complications, and cardiovascular events.
With this, it is imperative to address the gap in cross-sectional studies of viral illnesses like HIV in response to the changing landscape of the disease.
To address this, the DOST-PCHRD is supporting two (2) projects under Phil-DIAMOND.

Project 1 of the Phil-DIAMOND Program, aims to determine the proportion of Filipino HIV+ patients with neurocognitive and metabolic complications, as well as identify possible biomarkers or genetic mutations that codes for immune dysfunction and viral persistence.
This project is headed by Dr. Marissa M.
Alejandria of the University of the Philippines Manila, and in collaboration with the Hawaii Center for AIDS (HICFA) and Ndhlovu laboratory at the University of Hawaii in Manoa.

Meanwhile, Project 2 of the Phil-DIAMOND Program, headed by Dr. Ahmad Reza Mazahery of the University of the Philippines Diliman, aims to help improve the efforts of personalized medicine in the country.

The project aims to develop in vitro biological models that simulate the effects of immune biomarkers during the onset of conditions accelerated by HIV such as neuroinflammation and atherosclerosis, the condition of the thickening of arteries.
To date, Project 1 has established a fully-functioning Flow Cytometry Core Laboratory, a facility for the analysis and sorting of cells, in the UPM.
The facility is also envisioned to become a training ground for the DOST-PCHRD’s MD-PhD in Molecular Medicine scholars.
In support of the Laboratory’s human resources, flow cytometry and virological techniques have been institutionalized and included in the course syllabus of UPM.
In addition, blood samples and clinical data from study participants were collected, and DNA extraction protocols on human blood samples and immune marker panels have been optimized.
The extracted DNA from the collected samples will be sent to the Philippine Genome Center for sequencing.
At the same time, the team is continuously recruiting HIV+ patients for the study.
For Project 2, the team has completed the establishment and development of Mammalian Cell Culture Laboratory-Stem Cell In Vitro Applications in Research and Modeling (MCCL-SCIARM) in UPD.

This disease modeling laboratory will help in training undergraduate and graduate students, and MD-PhD/Ph.D. students whose research interests include cellular disease modeling, advanced molecular biology techniques, and infectious disease pathogenesis.
Moreover, a satellite disease modeling laboratory is being developed at the Mindanao State University - Iligan Institute of Technology (MSU-IIT) in Iligan City.

The project team also conducted various inter-program training and workshops on flow cytometry, disease modeling, cell culture, and natural product extraction, as well as completed the training of personnel for induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) generation at Cambridge, United Kingdom hosted by StemCell Technologies.
To date, Dr. Mazahery’s team has successfully generated the first-ever iPSCs from Filipino cells.
The completion of this experiment will complete the disease models for HIV-related neurocognitive disorders and metabolic complications.
By the end of implementation, the outputs of the program can provide awareness and knowledge on the current burden of HIV-related complications.

Through the comprehensive test for neurocognitive performance, the results of the study can also provide normative scores that can be used for the diagnosis of HIV-associated neurocognitive disease (HAND) and other neurodegenerative conditions.

Ultimately, the findings can provide possible recommendations for the standard of care for people living with HIV which could be made in terms of screening for neurocognitive impairment, as well as monitoring of immune dysfunction levels.
More importantly, possible biobanking of the first-ever Filipino-derived iPSCs will provide a safer and more personalized way to study the mechanisms of HIV.
The success in developing iPSCs can be used as a disease model not only for HIV, but also to other known diseases that are of high morbidity rate.

To address the research gaps on how ethical standards in human participants research are embedded among social science research organization and researchers in the Philippines and how codes of ethics are implemented in research community and affect researchers, Dr. Lourdes M.

Portus of the Philippine Social Science Council implemented the project entitled, “Mainstreaming Ethics in Human-Participant Research: Perspectives and Practices of Social Science Research Organizations and Researchers in the Philippines." The project investigated how codes and principles of ethics have been embedded, enforced, and implemented among research organizations and researchers’ ethical mindset and behavior to protect the dignity, rights and wellbeing of participants.

Through online surveys, key informant interviews, and focus group discussions, the project determined the following: 1.  presence of an internal code of ethics to participating research organizations, plans and challenges of organizations in creating an internal code of ethics; 2.  effects of the absence of a code of ethics in monitoring compliance with ethical research practice; and 3.  how research organizations implement ethical standards and codes in human-participant research and incorporate data privacy protection in their code of ethics.
Completed on 12 August 2023, the project was able to produce a set of infographics containing the rationale of the study, major findings, identified challenges, and policy recommendations.

To cope up with new challenges and demands in reviewing research protocols, Research Ethics Committees (RECs) need to update their systems and practices, hence the implementation of a project entitled, “Benchmarking study on comparable standards and ethics review procedures in countries with systems or practices that can serve as models for further improvement.” Led by Dr. Cristina E.

Torres of the University of the Philippines Manila, the project explored the current state of the Philippine RECs including the utilization of tools and approaches in ethical review of research protocols, adoption of ethics oversight system, as well as the identification of best practices in terms of REC review procedures/performance and accreditation processes to support continual quality improvement.
In 2023, the project conducted an assessment of the local RECs' performance using the 2023 WHO Global Benchmarking tool.
Using the benchmarking scores, the gaps in the REC performance were identified.

The study found that there was full implementation in the aspects of REC structure/composition and REC procedures, while only partial implementation was noted for the criteria to wit, legal and regulatory framework, resources, transparency and accountability, monitoring of performances, and responsible research institutions.
Focus group discussions among RECs and other research stakeholders in the country were also conducted to obtain opinions on REC practices and accreditation processes.

The primary care model is a model of care that enables first-contact healthcare to be accessible to patients.

Through this study, the group of Dr. Antonio Miguel Dans is piloting the primary care model in corporate, rural, and urban settings in the Philippines by testing the Philippine Health Insurance Corp. (PhilHealth) primary care financing system.

Generally, the study aimed to evaluate the effect of shifting to a comprehensive universal social health insurance-funded primary care system across the following outcome areas: • Utilization of benefits; • Patient satisfaction; • Health care provider satisfaction; • Health care worker knowledge; • Quality of care; • Health outcomes; • Financial risk protection; and • Administration and governance .Based on these criteria, the team reported positive results in improving the accessibility and use of primary care.
Results of the study may be used as a reference in further establishing a primary care model in the country, which could support the implementation of Universal Health Care.

The need for fast and efficient review at the national levels of vaccine-related research protocols was underscored during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Answering to this need is the DOH-Single Joint Research Ethics Board (SJREB), the body designated as the central research ethics committee to review COVID-19 vaccine-related protocols.

With the COVID-19 experience highlighting lessons and gaps in the ethics regulatory system, this study by Ms. Edlyn Jimenez assesses the impact of the single joint ethics review process on the current ethics review system in the country.
Site visits were conducted to assess the status of SJREB operational efficiency and readiness for the PHREB Level 3 Accreditation which covers documents in 2021, 2022, 2023.
Data is now being completed and cleaned for analysis.
Recommendations will be made regarding the current status of SJREB.
Results of the study will serve as a guide in ensuring a well-defined regulatory system through the SJREB with functions and scopes of authority properly defined.
The REACH Program was launched in 2023 to undertake activities on all epidemiology-related research and development priorities of the DOH.
Through this, the epidemiology and surveillance policies will be informed with different sets of evidence to ensure its relevance, comprehensibility, and sustainability among its end users.
The program utilized Php 20,836,304.89 of funding this year.
Enhancing the country’s epidemiological and surveillance capacities through innovative digital solutions is among the priorities of the DOH.

Collaborating closely with the Ateneo Center for Computing Competency and Research (ACCRE), the DOH- Epidemiology Bureau (EB) developed the Feasibility Analysis of Syndromic Surveillance Using Spatio-Temporal Epidemiological ModeleR (FASSSTER) model.
Currently, the FASSSTER serves as a disease modeling and surveillance tool for COVID-19.

This project led by Dr. Timothy Robin Teng aims to enhance FASSSTER’s current surveillance of notifiable diseases using epidemiological disease modeling in the country for the use of both national and local governments.
Specifically, it aims to generate COVID-19 projections, develop a dengue model, migrate the FASSSTER to the servers of the DOH, and build capacities of DOH staff in disease modeling initiatives.
In 2023, the team identified the prerequisites for the development of the enhanced FASSSTER system while gathering further system requirements and inventory of technology resources are ongoing.
They were also able to gain feedback and insights for determining the system functional and non-functional requirements.

The Design Thinking Workshop and the Stakeholder's Meeting was also conducted where the team submitted capacity building proposals on the FASSSTER training manual, FASSSTER system maintenance manual, MS Program integrating components of FASSSTER, and Executive Program for Use of Modeling in Policy Making.
Chronic Hepatitis B and C remain as the leading causes of liver-related morbidity and mortality from liver cirrhosis and liver cancer among Filipinos.
Vital in improving health policy against the disease are updated and accurate data on the burden of disease, particularly, its seroprevalence and disease severity.
The 2023 National Nutrition Survey (NNS) is an opportunity to collect this important information exactly 20 years from the last available seroprevalence survey conducted in 2003.

Conducting the seroprevalence survey in conjunction with the 2023 NNS will allow time-, personnel-, and cost-efficiency in getting the estimates of HBV and HCV seroprevalence in the general adult population.
Deriving the necessary data from the survey will help determine the prevalence and associated clinicodemographic factors of chronic Hepatitis B Virus and Hepatitis CV infection among adults.

To provide data on youth tobacco consumption and tobacco use initiation, the team of Dr. Agnes Pacho will conduct the 7th Round of the Global Youth Tobacco Survey (GYTS) and 6th round of the Global School-based Student Health Survey (GSHS) for the school year 2023- 2024.

The GYTS will assess tobacco use among 13–to 15-year-old students and their knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors toward tobacco use; while, the GSHS aspect aims to assess the behavioral risk and protective factors related to the leading causes of morbidity and mortality among 13–17-year-old students.
Data collected from the survey will help inform national tobacco prevention and control programs, and facilitate the comparison of tobacco-related data at the national, regional and global levels.
Some individuals who recovered from COVID-19 infection have been reported to experience prolonged symptoms of the disease.
Common persisting symptoms include fatigue, loss of smell or taste, depression or anxiety, memory or concentration problems, among many.

The condition of experiencing symptoms despite recovery is known as “Long COVID-19.” People suffering from this may have difficulty functioning in everyday life, negatively affecting one’s quality of life, as well as individual and organizational productivity.
Due to this, long COVID-19 proves to be an important illness to be investigated.

Addressing the lack of epidemiologic data on post-COVID conditions in the Philippines, Dr. John Robert Medina initiated a project to describe the epidemiology of post-COVID symptoms among Filipinos in selected occupational groups.

Particularly, the study will focus on occupational health nurses and occupational health physicians, municipal health officers and rural health physicians, and teaching and non-teaching personnel of basic and higher education.
This project is envisioned to provide evidence for the government and labor institutions to develop health-promoting policies and programs for Filipino workers.
The Philippines remains to be one of the lowest spending per capita in healthcare relative to its Southeast Asia (SEA) neighbor countries, and by global standards.
This is despite the increased public spending in healthcare and higher reliance on pharmaceutical products.
Private payments drive the majority of healthcare spending at approximately 55%, and come as a burden to the population, especially those in the low affordability bands.
Consistent with healthcare spending, the pharmaceutical sector is skewed towards out-of-pocket payments and the private sector.
The private sector is highly fragmented and has a strong monetary element, leading to uncontrolled and high drug prices.

Amid rising inflation, the Maximum Drug Retail Price (MDRP) for drugs and medicines was implemented through EO No 104 s. 2020 and EO No 155 s. 2021 to measure, monitor, and control drug prices in the country.
To assess the current implementation of the legislation, a tie-up program between the DOST-PCHRD and the DOH-Pharmaceutical Division (PD) was forged.
In 2023, the program utilized Php 711,729.37 from its allocated funds.

PhilHealth, committed to achieving Universal Health Care (UHC) since its inception in 1995, has actively pursued this goal through the PhilHealth STUDIES project.

Established in collaboration with DOST-PCHRD in 2015, the project aims to fortify health research management, efficiently allocate resources, generate pertinent research studies, and enhance research capacity.

Under the four main components overseen by the Council—Research Services, Research Dissemination, Capacity Building, and Administrative Support—the project contributed significantly in 2023, supporting seven research projects, organizing a research forum, conducting a Capacity Building activity, and facilitating five research dissemination activities.
These efforts are integral to advancing evidence-based policy reforms and fostering informed decision-making within PhilHealth programs and services.
In 2023, PhilHealth STUDIES’s research services focused on studying the members' experience, evaluating health policy reforms, and expanding health service coverage.

The program yielded three completed projects, including a Client Awareness and Satisfaction Survey conducted by Novo Trends PH, Inc., which revealed improved satisfaction ratings and recommended expansions in coverage and services.

Another project, the PhilHealth Share Ratio Study by Health Futures Foundation, Inc., highlighted the reliance of health facilities on PhilHealth funds and proposed strategic changes to address inefficiencies.

Additionally, the Policy Research and Development project led by the Ateneo School of Government aimed at creating standards for third-party accreditation mechanisms, producing toolkits recommended for nationwide implementation in 2023.

The research findings were disseminated in the 7th PhilHealth STUDIES Forum, on 17 November 2023, at the Philippine International Convention Center, Pasay City which gathered 159 participants both onsite and online to discuss health financing and Universal Health Care.

The forum was preceded by the Talakayang HeaRT Beat press conference held in June 2023, amplifying public awareness of PhilHealth's R&D activities in collaboration with DOST-PCHRD and partner institutions.
Media coverage included major outlets such as ABS-CBN, GMA News, News5, DOSTv, PTV, and The Manila Times.
In terms of capacity building, two Research Associates were appointed to PhilHealth's Corporate Planning Department in 2023, contributing to small-scale studies.
These studies addressed issues such as the impact of the 45-day Benefit Rule and the rationalization of the 90-day Single Period of Confinement.

Led by Dr. Sharia Laine de Paz-Silava, the University of the Philippines Manila spearheads a project that will assess the effectiveness of Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) vaccination in Filipino children.
It aims to evaluate antibody responses against JEV, Dengue Virus (DENV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) before and after vaccination.
Currently in its second year, it involves 40 Filipino mother-infant pairs as participants.
The recruitment process included briefing, eligibility checks, and consent acquisition, followed by immunization and blood collection before and after vaccination.
Samples were transferred to the University of the Philippines Manila for processing and later shipped to the National Chung Hsing University (NCHU) in Taiwan for laboratory analysis.

With a total support of Php 4,757,836.60 from DOST-GIA Program, the study is now conducting a Plaque Reduction Neutralization Test (PNRT) to assess neutralization activity against JEV, DENV, and ZIKV.
Statistical analyses will compare antibody levels pre- and post-vaccination and evaluate differences between children born to JEV-seronegative and JEV-seropositive mothers.
While bioactive compounds with potential as drug candidates are highly abundant and diverse in plant resources, some are limitedly used due to inefficient absorption of the compounds into the body.

An example of these underutilized compounds is syringic acid, a compound found in plants that have been shown to prevent chronic diseases such as diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and cerebral ischemia among other health benefits.

To enhance absorption in the body, the team of Dr. Joshua Santos of the Department of Science and Technology-Industrial Technology and Development Institute (DOST-ITDI) is exploring the use of metal organic framework or MIL-100(Fe), a material that may be used as a drug carrier, for syringic acid.
Under the project, capacity building efforts for the team such as training exchange programs focused on the synthesis of the MIL-100(Fe) and laboratory tours will be conducted.
Necessary equipment for the conduct of the research have also been purchased.
The successful development of drug carriers for syringic acid will enable the utilization of the compound as a treatment for various diseases.

Soil-transmitted helminths (STH) infection, or more commonly known as intenstinal worm infection, remains highly prevalent in the rural and poor urban communities in the Philippines.

The infection spreads through contact with water bodies that are contaminated with the worm larvae emerging from snail hosts, which shows that the environment and animals play a significant role in the spread of intestinal helminths to humans.

Researchers from the University of Los Banos led by Dr. Vachel Gay Paller, and from the University of Surrey, United Kingdom led by Dr. Martha Betson, collaborated to assess the impact of zoonotic transmission and environmental reservoirs on human intestinal infection in the Philippines.
The study shed light on the transmission dynamics of these parasites, specifically in endemic rural communities in Mindanao.
Using molecular tools, the investigators gained valuable insights on the associations between intestinal worms in humans and animalals, for helminth control and elimination efforts in these areas.

As the focal institution to the World Health Organization’s Western Pacific Region Index Medicus (WPRIM), the Council assists Philippine journals to be indexed under the WHO WPRIM through its role in the National Journal Selection Committee.
The Committee reviewed journal applicants and recommended the Philippine Journal of Pathology to the WHO Regional Journal Selection Committee (RSJC) for inclusion in WPRIM.
The journal was approved for WPRIM inclusion during the RJSC Meeting in Vietnam in August 2023.

Furthering its efforts in strengthening health journal publishing in the country, the DOST-PCHRD participated in the annual meeting and conference of the Asia Pacific Association of Medical Journal Editors (APAME) on 18 August 2023 at Hue City, Vietnam.
In the gathering, the Council provided inputs on data contribution, regional information sharing, and its current initiatives on health journal publishing.

The Council reported its best practices on health research information dissemination including ongoing HERDIN partnerships with local journals and institutions, HERDIN orientation and learning sessions, conduct of national medical writing workshops in partnership with the Philippine Association of Medical Journal Editors (PAMJE), and funding support given to the project "Enhancing Research Dissemination via the Development of an Efficient Web-based Journal Management System (E-REVIEW)." The project aims to enhance research dissemination by creating an online automated system for the submission of manuscripts, online review process, and timely publication of the PIDSP Journal.
